name: Shakti
summary: Raj Comics' blue-skinned heroine, a housewife named Chanda whose body is used by the goddess Kali to deliver justice, often called the strongest in Raj's universe.
origin: Chanda is a simple housewife who learns that her husband has been killing their daughters. In the comics, her grief and anger draw the goddess Kali, who uses Chanda's body as a host to become Shakti and deliver justice, and Shakti kills the husband. Chanda goes back to hospital and social work, hiding her third eye under a headband she says is for migraines. Whenever women anywhere cry for help, she senses it and turns into Shakti.

firstAppearance.title: Two In One Issues #14 (Comics Religion record)

powers: Melts and reshapes metal with her mind
Senses the cries of women worldwide

storyline.title: A housewife's grief
storyline.beat: Chanda discovers her husband has been killing her daughters, and her anger calls out to the goddess.

storyline.title: Shakti awakens
storyline.beat: The goddess Kali uses Chanda's body as a host and becomes Shakti, who then deals with the husband.

storyline.title: Chanda and Shakti
storyline.beat: By day Chanda works in hospitals and social work, hiding her third eye; Shakti appears when women anywhere cry for help.

storyline.title: Misunderstood by heroes
storyline.beat: Early on she fights Nagraj, Dhruva, Doga, Parmanu, Anthony and Tiranga before the misunderstandings end.

storyline.title: Joining the Brahmand Rakshak
storyline.beat: She joins P.O.E.M. and the Brahmand Rakshak team, and gets team-up issues with Parmanu, Doga and Dhruva.

gossip.text: Raj Comics' Shakti is hosted by Chanda, a housewife through whom the goddess Kali acts, which is her core premise.
Her third eye is hidden under a headband that Chanda says she wears for migraines.
Shakti is simply Marvel's Thor with a new name.
gossip.truth: Sources say her plot was loosely adapted from Thor, but she is rooted in Indian faith: the goddess Kali using a housewife as host.

gossip.text: Raj Comics fans often call her the strongest character in its universe.
Chanda's Shakti form is said to be strong enough to lift an aeroplane and fly it at light speed.

quiz.q: In the comics, which goddess acts through Shakti?
quiz.why: Raj Comics presents Shakti as an incarnation of Kali using Chanda as host.

quiz.q: What did Shakti do at first when she met other Raj Comics heroes?
quiz.why: Early on she clashed with several Raj heroes through misunderstandings before they became allies.

quiz.q: Where does Chanda hide her third eye?
quiz.why: She covers it with a headband and says it is for migraines.

quiz.q: What does Shakti sense from far away?
quiz.why: She feels the cries and pain of women anywhere in the world.

theme.tagline: A cry across the world, a third eye opens.

timeline.title: Earliest recorded issue
timeline.note: Comics Religion records Two In One Issues number 14, dated January 1998, as her first appearance among its 97 listed.

timeline.title: Aa Shakti aa Parmanu
timeline.note: A library catalogue dates this Raj Comics special to 2000 and lists Parmanu as the other hero.

timeline.title: Kaal aur Doga
timeline.note: The catalogue dates this issue to 2004, pairing Shakti with Doga.

timeline.title: Dhruv-Shakti
timeline.note: The catalogue lists this 2008 issue alongside Super Commando Dhruva, a hero she once fought through a misunderstanding.

timeline.title: Angaarey
timeline.note: A catalogued 2012 edition teams Shakti with Parmanu and Doga in a trio story.

facts.text: Chanda hides her third eye beneath a headband and says it is for her migraines.
Besides fire and metal, she can split her body, change size, and even travel in time, as in the story Trikali.
Her plot is said to be loosely adapted from Marvel's Thor, but with Kali as the force that takes her over.
Early on she fought Nagraj, Dhruva, Doga, Parmanu, Anthony and Tiranga because of misunderstandings.
She is said to be strong enough to carry an aeroplane with ease and to fly it at the speed of light.

The origin image in the comics is that Chanda's horror at what her husband did builds like a volcano of anger, with smoke rising to the heavens, and that is what draws the goddess Kali to act through her.
Raj Comics has published 97 Shakti titles in all, some with playful names such as Shakti Help Me and Shakti Khatm (Shakti Ends).
Wikipedia describes the force behind Shakti as the anger of women across the world, and IndiaNetzone adds that this rage feeds the fire she wields, so her power grows from other people's pain.

Wikipedia compares Shakti to Marvel's Thor, who lived for a time as the mortal doctor Donald Blake. Likewise, Chanda lives an ordinary hospital and social-work life until she changes into her godlike self.
Some of her comics are named after the heroes she joins forces with, such as Doga Shakti, Parmanu Shakti and Dhruva Shakti, so the cover title tells you who she is teaming up with.
Raj Comics lists a Kaliyug series starring Shakti, Nagraj and Super Commando Dhruva, and her own title list includes a Kalyug special, so she stars in a big three-hero crossover.
A library catalogue of Raj Comics dates Aa Shakti aa Parmanu to 2000 and Jaag Utha Shaitaan to 2002, both listing Parmanu as the other hero, so Shakti and Parmanu teamed up more than once.
The same catalogue lists Dhruv-Shakti in 2008 with Super Commando Dhruva, one of the heroes she fought early on, which shows how far those misunderstandings were left behind.
The catalogue dates the Angaarey special to 2012 and lists Parmanu and Doga alongside Shakti, a three-hero team-up, with the entry tagged as a superheroine story.

Raj Comics also published comics of Shaktimaan, the TV hero, and the Shakti title list includes a special called Sarv Shaktimaan. The sources do not say what happens in it, but its name plays on the shared word.
The titles hint at how wide her stories range: spooky names like Dayan and Pretaa, techy ones like Death Dot Com and Zero G, and patriotic ones like Border and Saare Jahan Se Uncha.
Raj Comics grew from a pulp-fiction publisher whose novels sold up to a million copies each. It became a comics house after the founder's sons dreamed of creating original Indian superheroes.

Raj Comics was founded in 1984 by Rajkumar Gupta, Manoj Gupta and Sanjay Gupta. It has produced close to 35,000 comics, mostly in Hindi, and sells hardcovers and motion comics as well as print and e-books.

Comics Religion lists her under the name Chandra, with her earliest record in Two In One Issues number 14 from January 1998 and 97 appearances. Wikipedia spells her name Chanda and also counts 97 titles.
IndiaNetzone puts Shakti in two groups, P.O.E.M. (Protectors of Earth and Mankind) and Brahmand Rakshak. Wikipedia compares Brahmand Rakshak to DC's Justice League.
Wikipedia's list of other Shakti appearances includes a Trendy Baba series book, number 3, titled Shakti, so she is the named star of at least one book in that series.

kidSummary: Shakti is a blue-skinned superheroine from Raj Comics. In the comics, the goddess Kali acts through a kind woman named Chanda, and together they help women and girls in danger anywhere in the world.

story.title: An ordinary woman
story.text: Chanda is a simple woman who works in a hospital and does social work. She hides a special third eye under a headband and says it is for headaches.

story.title: A cry for help
story.text: In the comics, when Chanda faces great wrong, the goddess Kali acts through her and she becomes Shakti. Her husband did terrible harm to their daughters, and Shakti makes sure he is stopped.

story.title: Hearing every cry
story.text: Whenever a woman anywhere in the world calls out for help, Chanda can sense it and change into Shakti.

story.title: Powers beyond belief
story.text: Shakti can turn into light, fly at light speed, melt metal with her mind and even lift an aeroplane.

story.title: Friends at last
story.text: At first she clashed with Nagraj, Dhruva and Doga because of misunderstandings. Later she joined them in the Brahmand Rakshak, the protectors of the universe.
